name: Anime and Manga
description: Japanese comics and animation, from Astro Boy and Doraemon to Dragon Ball, Studio Ghibli, Pokémon and One Piece.

checkpoints.name: Origins
checkpoints.note: Japanese printmakers of the floating world sold cheap, lively pictures to city crowds. In 1814 Katsushika Hokusai published the first volume of his sketchbooks titled Manga, a word that later came to mean Japanese comics.

checkpoints.name: The first anime and Astro Boy
checkpoints.note: Anime starts as short animated films in the 1910s. After the war, Osamu Tezuka launches Astro Boy in 1952, a boy robot whose large eyes and long serial stories set the pattern for manga and anime.

checkpoints.name: Weekly magazines
checkpoints.note: Weekly Shonen Jump starts in 1968 and becomes a home for serial adventures read by millions of young people. Doraemon, a robot cat from the future, arrives in 1969, and Hello Kitty appears in 1974.

checkpoints.name: Akira, Dragon Ball and Studio Ghibli
checkpoints.note: Akira begins as a manga in 1982 and Dragon Ball in 1984. In 1985 Hayao Miyazaki and his colleagues found Studio Ghibli, whose films carry anime to world audiences.

checkpoints.name: Worldwide hits
checkpoints.note: Sailor Moon (1991), Detective Conan (1994), One Piece (1997) and Naruto (1999) each run for years and are translated into many languages. Spirited Away (2001), from Studio Ghibli, later wins an Academy Award, and Death Note (2003) shows a dark thriller can sell too.

checkpoints.name: The streaming era
checkpoints.note: Pokémon Go, released in 2016, puts a Japanese monster-collecting franchise onto phones around the world, a sign of how far these characters have travelled. Magazines still serialise new stories, while streaming carries anime to audiences in many countries.
